stories.title: AIIMS performs India's first open fetal surgery
stories.summary: Doctors at AIIMS New Delhi performed India's first open fetal surgery on 12 November. The six-hour procedure repaired a lumbosacral myelomeningocele in a 25-week fetus. More than 30 clinicians participated in the operation, which the institute says offers a chance to reduce neurological damage before birth.

stories.title: Government health spending triples over a decade
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry reports that public health expenditure rose from 1.30 lakh crore to 4.14 lakh crore between 2013 and 2024. During the same period, the share of healthcare costs paid directly by households fell from 64.2 percent to 42.7 percent, according to national estimates.

Govt health spending triples, household burden eases | Today News

stories.title: Analysis links air pollution to broad health impacts
stories.summary: An analysis of 180 epidemiological studies conducted in India between 1975 and 2025 found that 91 percent reported adverse health associations with air pollution. The findings suggest impacts extend beyond respiratory issues to include diabetes, pregnancy complications, and neurocognitive disorders, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean

stories.title: Telangana sets 2028 target for new public health institute
stories.summary: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy laid the foundation stone for the Public Health Foundation of India campus in Hyderabad on 14 November. The project has a completion target of 2 June 2028. The Chief Minister has offered to serve as the institution’s brand ambassador.

stories.title: Study finds causal link between pollution and mental health
stories.summary: A 2023 macroanalysis published in The Journal of Development Studies identified a causal link between air pollution and poor mental health. The study, which sampled 21,203 individuals across six states, suggests that seasonal smog events provide a critical window for clinicians to screen patients for mental health issues.

stories.title: 1 in 5 children with diabetes face mental health challenges
stories.summary: A PGI study of 97 children with Type 1 Diabetes found that 20 percent experience significant psychological maladjustment. While average mental health scores were comparable to the local population, depression showed a strong link to long-term blood sugar levels. The findings were published in a medical journal.

stories.title: Telangana CM unveils master plan for public health institute
stories.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy laid the foundation for the PHFI Institute of Public Health Sciences. He assured entrepreneurs of full government support, stating that specific frameworks are in place to provide land, water, and infrastructure. The state government aims to eliminate policy confusion for investors.

stories.title: AIIMS Patna hosts walkathon for World Diabetes Day
stories.summary: The Department of General Medicine at AIIMS Patna observed World Diabetes Day with a walkathon and public awareness programme. The event involved faculty, nursing professionals, and administrative staff to promote early diagnosis and disease management. The walk concluded at the hospital's outpatient foyer.

stories.title: Uttarakhand to open AIIMS satellite centre in Kichha
stories.summary: Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami announced that a new AIIMS satellite centre in Kichha will soon be dedicated to the public. The facility is intended to improve healthcare access within the state and reduce the need for residents to travel long distances for medical treatment.

stories.title: Air pollution linked to multiple health issues in India - NewsBytes
AIIMS proposes national registry for poisoning cases
stories.summary: AIIMS New Delhi plans to transform its National Poisons Information Centre into a national network for toxicology. The proposed registry would digitally link poison-control units to track emerging trends and establish a national antidote bank. The system aims to improve real-time reporting and national preparedness.

stories.title: Africa CDC warns of worsening Ebola outbreak in Congo
stories.summary: Six months after the Ebola outbreak was declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Africa CDC director Jean Kaseya says the situation remains out of control. With over 11,200 cases and 5,500 deaths recorded, officials warn it could become the world's worst Ebola outbreak.

stories.title: Brazil reports first mpox death of 2026
stories.summary: Brazil has recorded its first mpox death of 2026. Despite the fatality, a public health institute stated that officials are not currently treating the recent surge in cases as an outbreak.

stories.title: Ebola containment efforts falter in Congo
stories.summary: Six months into the response, the Ebola outbreak in Congo remains out of control. Containment efforts are reportedly faltering as the disease continues to spread.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak reaches 11,145 cases
stories.summary: The 2026 Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 11,145 cases and 5,437 deaths. The CDC reports no associated cases in the U.S. and maintains that the risk to the American public remains low. Travel restrictions from affected regions remain in effect.

stories.title: Congo Ebola outbreak death toll nears 5,500
stories.summary: Six months after the outbreak began, Congo's Ebola crisis remains out of control with over 11,000 cases recorded. Nearly half of those infected have died, making it the deadliest of the country's 17 recorded outbreaks. Basic containment measures like contact tracing are struggling to keep pace.

stories.title: U.S. loses measles-free status
stories.summary: The Pan American Health Organization has revoked the measles-elimination status of the United States after 26 years. The decision follows a year of continuous transmission and the highest number of cases in three decades. Some 7,500 people have been infected and 13 have died.

stories.title: Weight-loss drug impacts fetal oxygen in sheep study
stories.summary: A single dose of semaglutide reduced heart output and uterine blood flow in pregnant sheep within two hours. Oxygen levels in the fetal bloodstream dropped, which researchers attributed to a decrease in the mother's overall blood output. The drug is currently used by millions for weight loss.

stories.title: Researchers urge focus on health in nuclear risk discussions
stories.summary: Editors from over 100 international journals have published a joint editorial calling for health professionals to prioritize health in public discussions regarding nuclear risk. The appeal comes in response to rising geopolitical tensions.

stories.title: U.S. loses measles elimination status
stories.summary: The United States has lost its global measles elimination status as outbreaks become more frequent. Public health experts note that the country failed to end sporadic outbreaks within a one-year window. Pennsylvania is currently managing one of the largest outbreaks seen in three decades.

stories.title: Global health authorities confirm U.S. lost measles elimination status
stories.summary: The U.S. has officially lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, a designation held for 25 years. The Pan American Health Organization concluded that the virus has reestablished regular transmission. The status is lost when sporadic outbreaks are not contained within a year.

stories.title: Mosquitoes identified in Tampa Bay dengue outbreak
stories.summary: The city is currently managing a dengue outbreak. Local health authorities are monitoring the mosquito populations responsible for the spread of the virus.

stories.title: Measles cases are gaining a foothold again in Minnesota - Star Tribune
Digital health risks and climate change discussed in Bengaluru
stories.summary: The Digital Transformations for Health Lab called for safe digital spaces, responsive health systems and improved knowledge to navigate them at a forum in Bengaluru. The event focused on the intersection of digital health risks and climate change. Digital spaces are now a primary topic of discussion.

stories.title: Web-based resource developed for transgender older adults
stories.summary: Researchers from the University of Virginia and Mount Sinai developed a web-based digital health resource to support healthcare decision-making for transgender and gender diverse older adults. The project used a co-design framework to center the lived experiences and priorities of the participants during the research process.

stories.title: Beyeonics Surgical seeks insolvency
stories.summary: Medical device company Beyeonics Surgical has filed for insolvency in Haifa District Court after accumulating $5.47 million in debt. The company holds approximately $50,000 in cash. Most of the debt is owed to shareholders who provided loans to finance operations. The company is now officially insolvent.

stories.title: Digital Health Africa seeks communications lead
stories.summary: Digital Health Africa is hiring a media and communications lead to shape digital visibility and promote innovation across the continent. The organization focuses on journalism, research and ecosystem development. It aims to advance digital health through capacity building and knowledge sharing across the African continent.

stories.title: AIIMS Nagpur and IIIT Pune sign health AI agreement
stories.summary: AIIMS Nagpur and IIIT Pune have signed a memorandum of understanding for joint research and faculty-student exchange in health technology. The agreement focuses on medical data analytics, AI and digital diagnostics. Medical and engineering institutes are increasingly pairing up to build capacity in health and AI.

stories.title: Digital health tools show modest postpartum benefits
stories.summary: A systematic review of 21 randomized controlled trials involving 4,121 participants found that digital health interventions offer modest improvements in physical activity and weight measures for postpartum women. The study suggests these platforms may help address maternal health vulnerabilities during a period of decreased physical activity.

stories.title: Caribbean and Taiwan health leaders review digital integration
stories.summary: Public health leaders from the Caribbean and Taiwan met in St. Lucia to discuss chronic disease management and digital health integration. The seminar reviewed preliminary data from the i-Screen initiative and examined achievements made under a regional capacity building project for the prevention of metabolic chronic diseases.

stories.title: Six Nigerian students earn distinctions in digital health
stories.summary: Six Nigerian postgraduate students graduated with distinctions in MSc Digital Health from Bournemouth University on November 3, 2026. The graduates attributed their academic success to peer support and collaborative learning. The group completed their studies in the United Kingdom.

stories.title: Healthcare organizations lag in AI model monitoring
stories.summary: CHIME's 2026 report found that 93.2 percent of surveyed healthcare organizations use AI, with full generative AI adoption reaching 54.8 percent. However, only 16.4 percent of users fully document model monitoring after deployment. Governance remains the next task for hospital IT leaders.

stories.title: GSMA Africa launches digital health index
stories.summary: GSMA Africa, the African Population and Health Research Center and the Science for Africa Foundation launched the Digital Health Index and a report on data systems. The initiative aims to promote African agency and collaboration in shaping the continent's data infrastructure and knowledge future.

stories.title: Researchers trial AI coach for diabetes
stories.summary: Researchers are testing an AI coach to help patients with type 2 diabetes maintain consistent healthy habits. Managing the condition requires long-term commitment to exercise and diet, but the quiet progression of the disease can make it easy for healthy intentions to slip.

stories.title: Australia to refresh digital inclusion target
stories.summary: Australia is set to miss its 2026 target for equal digital inclusion for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. A working group has been established to rewrite the goal. Digital health has been criticized for treating the issue as a telecommunications problem rather than a health one.

stories.title: Study links park visits to child mental health
stories.summary: Research from the University of Exeter tracking 4,219 children suggests that weekly trips to local parks may support better mental health. The study emphasized the need for high-quality, accessible parks. Social-emotional progress was tracked using parent-completed questionnaires across five stages of childhood.

stories.title: Study finds variability in autism brain activity
stories.summary: A study published in JNeurosci compared brain activity between individuals with autism spectrum disorder and those without. The research, led by the University of Iowa, identified remarkable variability in brain activity patterns among people with autism.

stories.title: Study explores Instagram and LGBTQ+ mental health
stories.summary: New research involving 478 LGBTQ+ adults in Israel examines the relationship between Instagram usage, discrimination and mental health. The study highlights the role of community support and cultural differences in how social media platforms impact the mental well-being of LGBTQ+ individuals.

stories.title: Gen X health study finds decline compared to boomers
stories.summary: Research from the UCL Centre for Longitudinal Studies on 8,000 participants found that Gen Xers experience worse physical and mental health than previous generations. This decline persists despite modern health education and pharmaceutical availability. The generation is reportedly less healthy than their boomer counterparts.

stories.title: Schizophrenia study examines perception of time
stories.summary: A study explores how people with schizophrenia-spectrum conditions experience time and space differently. The research suggests that brain energy mismatches may contribute to fragmented perceptions of time and feelings of disconnection from familiar surroundings. The phenomenon is more pronounced than in the general population.

stories.title: Stopping GLP-1 Weight-Loss Drugs? Study Flags Nearly Double Risk Of Heart Attack, Stroke And Death - News18
Recent police abuse linked to stigma and mental health in Russian cohort
stories.summary: An observational study in St. Petersburg found that recent police abuse among people living with HIV who inject drugs is associated with increased substance use stigma, depression, and anxiety. The study found no statistically significant association between these encounters and recent HIV medical care utilization.

stories.title: Karnataka High Court asks security and police to review mental health policies
stories.summary: The High Court of Karnataka has advised security and police organisations to prioritise the mental health of personnel carrying firearms. The order followed the quashing of criminal proceedings against a CISF sub-inspector who attempted to end her life while on duty due to severe personal distress.

stories.title: AI innovations for mental health: Ethics and inclusion
stories.summary: Research suggests AI interventions can reduce mental health symptoms and improve care access. Concerns persist regarding the safety and psychological risks of human-like AI systems. Experts note that viewing the field solely through the lens of conversational chatbots may be misleading for the future of care.

stories.title: Insomnia linked to higher risk of dementia, suicide and stroke
stories.summary: A study published in Sleep Medicine Reviews analyzed 20 review studies involving millions of participants and found insomnia linked to a 26 percent increased risk of stroke. The findings indicate a correlation with several major health issues but do not prove that insomnia directly causes them.

stories.title: ADHD effects on breathing, perception and behaviour
stories.summary: New research presented at the Neuroscience 2026 meeting indicates that attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder influences both mental and physical health across the human life span. The findings were shared at the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience.

stories.title: New biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease and depression
stories.summary: Researchers have developed new biomarkers intended to enhance the ability of clinicians to detect and treat disorders of the nervous system. These include applications for Alzheimer's disease, mood disorders, and neurodevelopmental conditions, as presented at the Neuroscience 2026 meeting.

research.title: A common osteoporosis drug blocked spinal damage in a surprising new study
research.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising genetic connection to spinal degeneration and found that an existing osteoporosis drug can prevent damaging mineral buildup in zebrafish spines. The discovery could pave the way for new treatments that slow or prevent a major cause of chronic back pain.

research.title: A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections
research.summary: A surprising discovery from Rockefeller University suggests that a common amino acid could play a powerful role in protecting against cancer and viral infections. Scientists found that low arginine levels interfere with the immune system's ability to recognize dangerous cells, while increasing arginine intake reduced colon cancer tumors.

research.title: Alzheimer’s may start shrinking two brain regions years before memory loss
research.summary: Johns Hopkins scientists have uncovered hidden warning signs of Alzheimer’s disease that may appear up to a decade before memory loss begins. Brain scans revealed that two regions involved in memory and emotion start shrinking before the hippocampus, the area doctors typically examine for signs of Alzheimer’s. These.

research.title: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds
research.summary: Scientists have discovered that vitamin C may help prevent potentially cancer-causing chemicals from forming in the stomach after eating foods containing nitrates and nitrites. A new mathematical model suggests that taking vitamin C after meals could reduce these harmful reactions, offering a possible new strategy for lowering cancer.
